entries.difference: Benchmarks quantum models against tuned classical ones under a calibration- and noise-aware attribution protocol; its surviving advantages are measured against a random-feature surrogate, and no rival receives the quantum map's own geometry.
entries.pool_title: How Quantum Is the Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- and Noise-Aware Benchmark and Attribution Audit of Quantum Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection
entries.title: How Quantum Is the Advantage? A Fair, Calibration- and Noise-Aware Benchmark and Attribution Audit of Quantum Machine Learning for Network Intrusion Detection

entries.difference: Audits quantum-kernel methods as a family across datasets and reports where they fail; it compares kernel families rather than matching one rival to the quantum metric, and sweeps no alignment axis.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernel Methods under Scrutiny: A Benchmarking Study
entries.title: Quantum Kernel Methods under Scrutiny: A Benchmarking Study

entries.difference: Documents a vanishing advantage on a financial cross-section and attributes it to the data; we hold the data-generating process fixed and sweep the alignment between the target's interaction structure and the map's.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernels and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns: Anatomy of a Vanishing Advantage
entries.title: Quantum Kernels and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns: Anatomy of a Vanishing Advantage

entries.difference: Finds a quantum-kernel advantage inside frozen foundation-model embeddings, measured against classical kernels of a different metric rather than a rival built to receive the quantum geometry.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernel Advantage over Classical Collapse in Medical Foundation Model Embeddings
entries.title: Quantum Kernel Advantage over Classical Collapse in Medical Foundation Model Embeddings

entries.difference: Argues from a Fourier-frequency argument that public tabular data cannot support quantum advantage and offers a recipe; the claim is about datasets, ours is about where a matched rival is beaten on a controlled generator.
entries.pool_title: The Fourier Wall: Why Public Tabular Datasets Refuse Quantum Advantage, and a Certified Recipe for Where It Lives
entries.title: The Fourier Wall: Why Public Tabular Datasets Refuse Quantum Advantage, and a Certified Recipe for Where It Lives

entries.difference: Shows evaluation choices (splits, calibration, metrics) decide the reported outcome in one application domain; we fix the protocol and vary the geometry, and the package records the choices so they can be re-read.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do
entries.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do

entries.authors: Kakavand, S., Strohmeyer, C., Schlotter, M.
entries.difference: Benchmarks quantum-kernel SVMs against classical baselines on tabular data with a tuned but unmatched classical arm, so a better geometry and a quantum geometry are not separated.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machines Against Classical Baselines on Tabular Data: A Rigorous Empirical Study with Hardware Validation
entries.title: Benchmarking Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machines Against Classical Baselines on Tabular Data: A Rigorous Empirical Study with Hardware Validation

entries.difference: Compares quantum feature-encoding strategies with a QSVM on a binary task; encoding is varied at fixed data, whereas our design varies the data-side alignment against a fixed encoding family.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking Quantum Feature Encoding Strategies for Binary Classification with QSVM
entries.title: Benchmarking Quantum Feature Encoding Strategies for Binary Classification with QSVM

entries.difference: Asks whether quantum advantage has been achieved and reviews the evidence; a review of claims, with no controlled instrument able to falsify a specific advantage mechanism.
entries.pool_title: Has quantum advantage been achieved?
entries.title: Has Quantum Advantage Been Achieved?

entries.difference: Reads quantum advantage through tensor networks and identifies where classical representations suffice; it speaks to simulability, not to the test error of a quantum kernel against a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Advantage: a Tensor Network Perspective
entries.title: Quantum Advantage: A Tensor Network Perspective

entries.authors: Alavi, A., Kouchmeshki, F., Akhoundi, H.
entries.difference: Builds invariance audits for quantum kernels and a real-to-Hermitian taxonomy; the audit tests invariances of a map, while our question is whether the map beats a rival that inherits its metric.
entries.pool_title: Invariance Audits for Quantum Kernels and Variational Rewinding: A Real-to-Hermitian Taxonomy of Projector, Flag, Anchor, and Density Geometry
entries.title: Invariance Audits for Quantum Kernels and Variational Rewinding: A Real-To-Hermitian Taxonomy of Projector, Flag, Anchor, and Density Geometry

entries.difference: Gives a closed-form benchmark for fixed-map denoising networks; a closed form for a different task family, with no paired rival and no swept data-side axis.
entries.pool_title: Parity Floors in Quantum Denoisers: A Closed-Form Benchmark for Fixed-Map Denoising Networks
entries.title: Parity Floors in Quantum Denoisers: A Closed-Form Benchmark for Fixed-Map Denoising Networks

entries.difference: Stress-tests variational models on a cloud-microphysics dataset and finds the advantage hard to reach; a single-domain stress test rather than a map over a controlled grid with a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: How Hard Is Quantum Advantage? A Cloud Microphysics Stress Test for Variational Quantum Models
entries.title: How Hard Is Quantum Advantage? A Cloud Microphysics Stress Test for Variational Quantum Models

entries.authors: Agnihotri, V., Kaur, J., Kaushik, S.
entries.difference: Evaluates quantum-kernel methods on noisy radar data against classical kernels, with no metric-matched surrogate and no planted alignment.
entries.pool_title: Practical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Radar Micro-Doppler Classification on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) Hardware
entries.title: Practical Evaluation of Quantum Kernel Methods for Radar Micro-Doppler Classification on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) Hardware

entries.difference: Surveys the varieties of quantum advantage and their resource requirements; it catalogues advantage claims rather than testing one under a matched-rival protocol.
entries.pool_title: The vast world of quantum advantage
entries.title: The Vast World of Quantum Advantage

entries.difference: Learns in active quantum subspaces for a scalable hybrid advantage; the advantage comes from restricting the subspace, a mechanism our grid does not vary.
entries.pool_title: Learning with Active Quantum Subspaces: Scalable Hybrid Advantage without Full Quantum Data-Encoding
entries.title: Learning with Active Quantum Subspaces: Scalable Hybrid Advantage Without Full Quantum Data-Encoding

entries.difference: Separates trainability diagnostics from optimization claims and states which controls variational quantum studies owe; those controls are for optimization landscapes, and we adopt the lesson for a regression comparison instead.
entries.pool_title: From Trainability Diagnostics to Optimization Claims: Boundaries and Controls in Variational Quantum Optimization
entries.title: From Trainability Diagnostics to Optimization Claims: Boundaries and Controls in Variational Quantum Optimization

entries.authors: Zendejas-Morales, C., Saikia, D., Singh, U.
entries.difference: Mitigates exponential concentration with local and multi-scale strategies; a remedy for kernel degeneracy, while we ask what the degeneracy does to a comparison against a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: Local and Multi-Scale Strategies to Mitigate Exponential Concentration in Quantum Kernels
entries.title: Local and Multi-Scale Strategies to Mitigate Exponential Concentration in Quantum Kernels

entries.difference: Proves the ZZ feature map's kernel is an anisotropic Gaussian whose metric is the identity plus the signless Laplacian of the entanglement graph, and gives a closed-form classical surrogate; it reports two dataset points and states the failing regime only qualitatively, whereas we map the advantage over alignment and bandwidth with that surrogate as the rival.
entries.pool_title: The ZZ feature map induces a signless Laplacian metric: a closed-form classical surrogate for quantum kernel regression
entries.title: The ZZ Feature Map Induces a Signless Laplacian Metric: A Closed-Form Classical Surrogate for Quantum Kernel Regression

entries.difference: Predicts quantum-kernel collapse from the data's fractal dimension and gives a ceiling as a qubit budget; it predicts kernel death, not the sign of the advantage against a matched rival, which is our outcome.
entries.pool_title: Fractal dimension predicts quantum kernel collapse in angle-encoded data
entries.title: Fractal Dimension Predicts Quantum Kernel Collapse in Angle-Encoded Data

entries.authors: Shin, S., Sweke, R., Jeong, H.
entries.difference: Reads quantum kernels as entangled tensor kernels and unifies several map families; a representational identity, with no paired comparison against a rival holding the same metric.
entries.pool_title: New perspectives on quantum kernels through the lens of entangled tensor kernels
entries.title: New Perspectives on Quantum Kernels Through the Lens of Entangled Tensor Kernels

entries.difference: Shows quantum kernels are spectral tensor networks with a controlled bond dimension; a simulability construction, which we read as a mechanism witness rather than as a rival arm.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernels are Spectral Tensor Networks
entries.title: Quantum Kernels Are Spectral Tensor Networks

entries.authors: Gan, B., Leykam, D., Thanasilp, S.
entries.difference: Unifies trace-induced quantum kernels into one framework; the framework makes the map's form explicit but measures no advantage against a metric-matched classical kernel.
entries.pool_title: A Unified Framework for Trace-induced Quantum Kernels
entries.title: A Unified Framework for Trace-Induced Quantum Kernels

entries.authors: Kübler, J., Buchholz, S., Schölkopf, B.
entries.difference: Shows quantum kernels carry an inductive bias aligned with the group structure of the data; the bias is demonstrated at fixed bandwidth, and our grid sweeps bandwidth and phase convention as well.
entries.pool_title: The Inductive Bias of Quantum Kernels
entries.title: The Inductive Bias of Quantum Kernels

entries.difference: Gives the optimal algorithmic complexity of inference in quantum-kernel methods; a complexity statement about sampling, not a statistical comparison of test error.
entries.pool_title: Optimal algorithmic complexity of inference in quantum kernel methods
entries.title: Optimal Algorithmic Complexity of Inference in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.authors: Sáez-Ortuño, L., Forgas-Coll, S., Ferrara, M.
entries.difference: Develops convergence theory and separation bounds for quantum-kernel methods; the bounds are asymptotic and no finite-sample map of the advantage region is exhibited.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernel Methods: Convergence Theory, Separation Bounds and Applications to Marketing Analytics
entries.title: Quantum Kernel Methods: Convergence Theory, Separation Bounds and Applications to Marketing Analytics

entries.authors: Park, D., Blank, C., Petruccione, F.
entries.difference: Establishes a theory of the quantum kernel-based binary classifier, including its consistency; a fixed-map theory with no rival that receives the map's metric.
entries.pool_title: The theory of the quantum kernel-based binary classifier
entries.title: The Theory of the Quantum Kernel-Based Binary Classifier

entries.authors: Gil-Fuster, E., Eisert, J., Dunjko, V.
entries.difference: Shows which kernels are expressible by embedding quantum kernels and where they gain; expressivity of the map at one bandwidth, rather than advantage against a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: On the expressivity of embedding quantum kernels
entries.title: On the Expressivity of Embedding Quantum Kernels

entries.difference: Argues quantum kernel machines should move beyond scalar-valued kernels; a position about the class of kernels, while our question is whether a scalar-valued quantum kernel beats its metric-matched counterpart.
entries.pool_title: Position: Quantum Kernel Machines Should Move Beyond Scalar-Valued Kernels to Realize Their Potential
entries.title: Position: Quantum Kernel Machines Should Move Beyond Scalar-Valued Kernels to Realize Their Potential

entries.difference: Simulates quantum-classical dual kernels with tensor networks at scale; a simulation result bounding what can be simulated, not what a rival attains.
entries.pool_title: Scalable Tensor Network Simulation for Quantum-Classical Dual Kernel
entries.title: Scalable Tensor Network Simulation for Quantum-Classical Dual Kernel

entries.authors: Kamisoyama, K., Nagano, L., Terashi, K.
entries.difference: Reports double descent in quantum kernel ridge regression; the curve runs over model complexity at one geometry, whereas we fix complexity and sweep alignment.
entries.pool_title: Double Descent in Quantum Kernel Ridge Regression
entries.title: Double Descent in Quantum Kernel Ridge Regression

entries.difference: Finds double descent in quantum kernel methods and locates its onset; a complexity-axis result rather than an alignment-axis map.
entries.pool_title: Double descent in quantum kernel methods
entries.title: Double Descent in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.authors: Tomasi, J., Anthoine, S., Kadri, H.
entries.difference: Establishes benign overfitting for quantum kernels; a generalisation result under an assumption on the kernel, with no empirical advantage boundary.
entries.pool_title: Benign Overfitting with Quantum Kernels
entries.title: Benign Overfitting with Quantum Kernels

entries.difference: Constructs a scalable quantum kernel inside an SVM; scalability of the map, with the comparison against a tuned but unmatched classical arm.
entries.pool_title: Support Vector Machine with a Scalable Quantum Kernel
entries.title: Support Vector Machine with a Scalable Quantum Kernel

entries.authors: Guo, X., Dai, J., Krems, R.
entries.difference: Benchmarks quantum fidelity kernels inside Gaussian-process regression; the rival is a classical GP kernel family, not a surrogate built from the quantum metric.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking of quantum fidelity kernels for Gaussian process regression
entries.title: Benchmarking of Quantum Fidelity Kernels for Gaussian Process Regression

entries.difference: Places quantum kernels inside a radial-basis-function network and classifies; an architecture choice, and the classical arm receives no part of the quantum geometry.
entries.pool_title: Classification using quantum kernels in a radial basis function network
entries.title: Classification Using Quantum Kernels in a Radial Basis Function Network

entries.difference: Studies geodesics of quantum feature maps on the space of operators; the geometry of the map as a manifold, while our question is what that geometry buys against a rival that is given it.
entries.pool_title: Geodesics of Quantum Feature Maps on the Space of Quantum Operators
entries.title: Geodesics of Quantum Feature Maps on the Space of Quantum Operators

entries.difference: Surveys quantum feature encoding with practical guidelines; a survey of choices, with no controlled comparison against a metric-matched rival.
entries.pool_title: Feature Encoding in Quantum Machine Learning: A Survey and Practical Guidelines
entries.title: Feature Encoding in Quantum Machine Learning: A Survey and Practical Guidelines

entries.authors: Zang, O., Barrué, G., Quertier, T.
entries.difference: Benchmarks data-encoding methods for quantum machine learning over datasets; encoding families are compared with each other, and the classical arm is unmatched.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking data encoding methods in Quantum Machine Learning
entries.title: Benchmarking Data Encoding Methods in Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Searches for quantum embeddings that improve a downstream model; a search over maps with the classical rival held fixed across the search.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Embedding Search for Quantum Machine Learning
entries.title: Quantum Embedding Search for Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Compares data-encoding schemes for variational circuits and proposes a hybrid; the target is classification accuracy of one circuit family, not the advantage's boundary.
entries.pool_title: Data Encoding for VQC in Qiskit, A Comparison With Novel Hybrid Encoding
entries.title: Data Encoding for VQC in Qiskit, a Comparison with Novel Hybrid Encoding

entries.difference: Sets out the theory and practice of quantum data encoding; a treatment of encodings as objects, without a paired rival that inherits an encoding's metric.
entries.pool_title: From Bits to Qubits: The Theory and Practice of Quantum Data Encoding
entries.title: From Bits to Qubits: The Theory and Practice of Quantum Data Encoding

entries.difference: Meta-learns encoding selection for quantum-kernel methods; selection among encodings, where we instead sweep the data-side alignment at a fixed encoding and qubit count.
entries.pool_title: Qmes: Quantum Meta-Learning for Encoding Selection in Quantum Kernel Methods
entries.title: Qmes: Quantum Meta-Learning for Encoding Selection in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.difference: Designs hardware-aware quantum kernels with graph neural networks; the objective is hardware performance, and no metric-matched classical arm is fitted.
entries.pool_title: Hardware-Aware Quantum Kernel Design Based on Graph Neural Networks
entries.title: Hardware-Aware Quantum Kernel Design Based on Graph Neural Networks

entries.authors: Sharma, D., Singh, P., Kumar, A.
entries.difference: Studies the role of entanglement for enhancing quantum kernels in classification; the entanglement axis is varied, while we ask whether the resulting geometry can be given to the rival.
entries.pool_title: The role of entanglement for enhancing the efficiency of quantum kernels towards classification
entries.title: The Role of Entanglement for Enhancing the Efficiency of Quantum Kernels Towards Classification

entries.difference: Benchmarks loss functions for trainable quantum feature maps; a training-side comparison, whereas our comparison is between a map and a rival at matched capacity.
entries.pool_title: Benchmarking loss functions for trainable quantum feature maps
entries.title: Benchmarking Loss Functions for Trainable Quantum Feature Maps

entries.authors: Lin, G., Tanaka, T., Zhao, Q.
entries.difference: Gives structured unitary tensor-network representations for circuit-efficient data encoding; a construction that lowers encoding cost, with no advantage claim and no rival.
entries.pool_title: Structured Unitary Tensor Network Representations for Circuit-Efficient Quantum Data Encoding
entries.title: Structured Unitary Tensor Network Representations for Circuit-Efficient Quantum Data Encoding

entries.difference: Proposes a quantum topological data encoding; a new encoding whose evaluation is against classical topological descriptors, not against a metric-matched kernel.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Topological Data Encoding
entries.title: Quantum Topological Data Encoding

entries.authors: Vlasic, A., Solanki, P., Pham, A.
entries.difference: Analyses encoding of real-world data through feature maps and expanded pseudo-entropy; a diagnostic of encodings, with no advantage boundary and no matched-rival protocol.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Circuits, Feature Maps, and Expanded Pseudo-Entropy: Analysis of Encoding Real-World Data into a Quantum Computer
entries.title: Quantum Circuits, Feature Maps, and Expanded Pseudo-Entropy: Analysis of Encoding Real-World Data into a Quantum Computer

entries.difference: Searches for efficient quantum feature maps with an evolutionary, training-free procedure; the search is over maps, and the comparison is not against a rival given the chosen map's metric.
entries.pool_title: QuProFS: An Evolutionary Training-free Approach to Efficient Quantum Feature Map Search
entries.title: QuProFS: An Evolutionary Training-Free Approach to Efficient Quantum Feature Map Search

entries.difference: Argues the input side is a permanent bottleneck for quantum machine learning; a position about data rather than a measurement of where a matched rival is beaten.
entries.pool_title: The Input Problem: A Permanent Bottleneck for Quantum Machine Learning
entries.title: The Input Problem: A Permanent Bottleneck for Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Proves exponential concentration of quantum kernels and ties it to the map's geometry; concentration is the ceiling our large-bandwidth arm observes, and we read its effect on the comparison rather than on trainability.
entries.pool_title: Exponential concentration in quantum kernel methods
entries.title: Exponential Concentration in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.authors: Kairon, P., Jäger, J., Krems, R.
entries.difference: Establishes an equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum-kernel machine learning and barren plateaus in variational models; a theoretical equivalence, with no rival arm and no swept alignment.
entries.pool_title: Equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational algorithms
entries.title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration in Quantum Machine Learning Kernels and Barren Plateaus in Variational Algorithms

entries.authors: Alcântara, P., Morais, L., Chaves, R.
entries.difference: Gives a representation-theoretic framework that characterises barren plateaus; a characterisation of when gradients vanish, not of when a kernel loses to a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: A Representation-Theoretic Framework for Characterizing Barren Plateaus
entries.title: A Representation-Theoretic Framework for Characterizing Barren Plateaus

entries.difference: Studies trainability, expressivity and efficiency together for scalable quantum machine learning; the axes are the model's own, whereas our axes are the data-side alignment and the encoding bandwidth.
entries.pool_title: Scalable Quantum Machine Learning: Trainability, Expressivity and Efficiency
entries.title: Scalable Quantum Machine Learning: Trainability, Expressivity and Efficiency

entries.difference: Proves concentration bounds for intrinsic-dimension estimation with Gaussian kernels; a classical-kernel concentration result that bounds the behaviour of our isotropic baseline arm.
entries.pool_title: Concentration bounds for intrinsic dimension estimation using Gaussian kernels
entries.title: Concentration Bounds for Intrinsic Dimension Estimation Using Gaussian Kernels

entries.difference: Shows concentration of kernel matrices and applies it to spectral clustering; the concentration is of a classical kernel matrix as the sample grows, whereas ours is over the map's phase convention and bandwidth at fixed n.
entries.pool_title: Concentration of kernel matrices with application to kernel spectral clustering
entries.title: Concentration of Kernel Matrices with Application to Kernel Spectral Clustering

entries.difference: Uses Lie-algebraic subspace quantization to mitigate barren plateaus and enable zero-shot learning; a mitigation technique whose benefit is measured inside the variational setting, not against a matched classical rival.
entries.pool_title: Lie-Algebraic Subspace Quantization for Zero-Shot Quantum Learning and Barren-Plateau Mitigation
entries.title: Lie-Algebraic Subspace Quantization for Zero-Shot Quantum Learning and Barren-Plateau Mitigation

entries.difference: Builds trainable kernels for symmetry-structured data without exponential concentration; it shows concentration is avoidable by construction, which supports reading our large-bandwidth arm as a genuine collapse rather than a protocol artefact.
entries.pool_title: Quantum advantage without exponential concentration: Trainable kernels for symmetry-structured data
entries.title: Quantum Advantage Without Exponential Concentration: Trainable Kernels for Symmetry-Structured Data

entries.difference: Dequantizes supervised quantum machine learning with random Fourier features; the dequantization targets worst-case complexity, while we ask about average test error under a rival that holds the map's own metric.
entries.pool_title: On Dequantization of Supervised Quantum Machine Learning via Random Fourier Features
entries.title: On Dequantization of Supervised Quantum Machine Learning via Random Fourier Features

entries.authors: Sweke, R., Shin, S., Gil-Fuster, E.
entries.difference: Dequantizes variational quantum machine learning kernel-based, without random Fourier features; a complexity statement, and the resulting classical model is not fitted to the quantum metric in our sense.
entries.pool_title: Kernel-based dequantization of variational QML without Random Fourier Features
entries.title: Kernel-Based Dequantization of Variational QML Without Random Fourier Features

entries.difference: States the potential and the limitations of random Fourier features for dequantizing quantum machine learning; it bounds what a specific classical family can do, not what a metric-matched kernel does.
entries.pool_title: Potential and limitations of random Fourier features for dequantizing quantum machine learning
entries.title: Potential and Limitations of Random Fourier Features for Dequantizing Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Robustly dequantizes the quantum singular-value transformation and quantum machine learning algorithms; an algorithmic dequantization, with no comparison of kernel test error.
entries.pool_title: Robust Dequantization of the Quantum Singular value Transformation and Quantum Machine Learning Algorithms
entries.title: Robust Dequantization of the Quantum Singular Value Transformation and Quantum Machine Learning Algorithms

entries.authors: Shin, S., Teo, Y., Jeong, H.
entries.difference: Dequantizes quantum machine learning models with tensor networks; the surrogate is a tensor network, a different rival family from the closed-form metric-matched surrogate we use.
entries.pool_title: Dequantizing quantum machine learning models using tensor networks
entries.title: Dequantizing Quantum Machine Learning Models Using Tensor Networks

entries.difference: Studies dequantizability from inputs; it asks when an input distribution defeats dequantization, whereas we construct the input and the rival ourselves so the comparison is exact.
entries.pool_title: Dequantizability from inputs
entries.title: Dequantizability from Inputs

entries.authors: Isogai, N., Murao, M., Yamasaki, H.
entries.difference: Dequantizes diagonally weighted matrix functions in a quantum-inspired way; a matrix-function construction rather than a kernel-regression comparison.
entries.pool_title: A Quantum-Inspired Dequantization Method for Diagonally Weighted Matrix Functions: Application to Learning with Optimized Random Features
entries.title: A Quantum-Inspired Dequantization Method for Diagonally Weighted Matrix Functions: Application to Learning with Optimized Random Features

entries.difference: Aligns a quantum kernel with the target by stochastic gradient descent; alignment is an objective to be optimised, while we hold the map fixed and measure what its geometry is worth against a rival given it.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernel Alignment with Stochastic Gradient Descent
entries.title: Quantum Kernel Alignment with Stochastic Gradient Descent

entries.authors: Islam, M., Liu, D., Sarkar, D.
entries.difference: Shows manifold approximation leads to robust kernel alignment; a classical alignment result we use to argue that alignment is the right axis for a comparison.
entries.pool_title: Manifold Approximation leads to Robust Kernel Alignment
entries.title: Manifold Approximation Leads to Robust Kernel Alignment

entries.difference: Constructs feature maps for the Laplacian kernel and its generalisations; it makes graph-Laplacian metrics classically explicit, which is the construction our closed-form rival needs.
entries.pool_title: Feature maps for the Laplacian kernel and its generalizations
entries.title: Feature Maps for the Laplacian Kernel and Its Generalizations

entries.difference: Unifies spectral equivariance and geometric transport in reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces; a framework for kernels' geometry, with no quantum counterpart arm.
entries.pool_title: Spectral Equivariance and Geometric Transport in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces: A Unified Framework for Orthogonal Polynomial and Kernel Estimation
entries.title: Spectral Equivariance and Geometric Transport in Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces: A Unified Framework for Orthogonal Polynomial and Kernel Estimation

entries.difference: Applies quantum multiple-kernel learning to drug discovery; multiple-kernel combination is the technique, and the classical arm is not given the combined metric.
entries.pool_title: Q2SAR: A Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning Approach for Drug Discovery
entries.title: Q2SAR: A Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning Approach for Drug Discovery

entries.difference: Combines classical Morgan fingerprints with quantum multiple-kernel learning for ligand classification; the hybrid's gain is measured inside one application and against unmatched classical kernels.
entries.pool_title: QBioFusion-QSAR: Morgan-Anchored Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning for Small-Data Ligand Classification
entries.title: QBioFusion-QSAR: Morgan-Anchored Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning for Small-Data Ligand Classification

entries.difference: Overcomes classical bottlenecks in drug discovery with quantum multiple-kernel learning; a domain application whose classical arm does not receive the quantum metric.
entries.pool_title: $\mathtt{Q^2SAR}$: overcoming classical bottlenecks in drug discovery via quantum multiple kernel learning
entries.title: $\mathtt{Q^2SAR}$: Overcoming Classical Bottlenecks in Drug Discovery via Quantum Multiple Kernel Learning

entries.difference: Builds quantum-classical multiple-kernel learning; the quantum part enters as an additional kernel family, which is precisely the setup our matched rival isolates.
entries.pool_title: Quantum-Classical Multiple Kernel Learning
entries.title: Quantum-Classical Multiple Kernel Learning

entries.difference: Explores an implementation of a quantum learning pipeline for support vector machines; an implementation study, with a tuned classical SVM rather than a metric-matched rival.
entries.pool_title: Exploring an implementation of quantum learning pipeline for support vector machines
entries.title: Exploring an Implementation of Quantum Learning Pipeline for Support Vector Machines

entries.difference: Applies quantum kernel and HHL-based support vector machines to multi-class classification; the comparison includes classical SVMs but no surrogate holding the quantum metric.
entries.pool_title: Quantum kernel and HHL-based support vector machines for multi-class classification
entries.title: Quantum Kernel and HHL-based Support Vector Machines for Multi-Class Classification

entries.difference: Uses quantum-kernel SVMs for multispectral satellite cloud detection; an application with a classical SVM baseline, and no geometry-matched control.
entries.pool_title: Cloud Detection in Multispectral Satellite Images Using Support Vector Machines With Quantum Kernels
entries.title: Cloud Detection in Multispectral Satellite Images Using Support Vector Machines with Quantum Kernels

entries.difference: Estimates the number of shots needed by quantum-kernel methods in search of advantage; a sampling-cost analysis rather than a test-error comparison against a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: In Search of Quantum Advantage: Estimating the Number of Shots in Quantum Kernel Methods
entries.title: In Search of Quantum Advantage: Estimating the Number of Shots in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.difference: Proposes a resource-efficient quantum kernel; the resource is qubits and gates, while our resource question is whether the geometric information is separable from the quantum construction.
entries.pool_title: A Resource Efficient Quantum Kernel
entries.title: A Resource Efficient Quantum Kernel

entries.difference: Reviews quantum kernel methods as a class and their relation to classical kernels; a review that names the matched comparison as open, which our study performs.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Machine Learning: Quantum Kernel Methods
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning: Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.authors: Tanner, J., Kam, C., Wang, J.
entries.difference: Reviews non-variational supervised quantum-kernel methods; a survey of the family without a controlled advantage map.
entries.pool_title: Non-variational supervised quantum kernel methods: a review
entries.title: Non-Variational Supervised Quantum Kernel Methods: A Review

entries.authors: Ogunade, T., Kassim, T., Osaro, E.
entries.difference: Benchmarks quantum-inspired feature maps against their classical counterparts under a matched spectral design; the closest prior control, but the maps are quantum-inspired classical embeddings, not entangling quantum kernels with a phase-convention axis.
entries.pool_title: A Matched Spectral Benchmark of Quantum Inspired Feature Maps
entries.title: A Matched Spectral Benchmark of Quantum Inspired Feature Maps

entries.difference: Uses the Nyström approximation for preconditioning in kernel machines; a classical approximation scheme whose error is analysed for a fixed kernel, not compared with a quantum map.
entries.pool_title: On the Nystrom Approximation for Preconditioning in Kernel Machines
entries.title: On the Nystrom Approximation for Preconditioning in Kernel Machines

entries.difference: Randomises clustered Nyström for large-scale kernel machines; a scaling technique whose target is runtime, not advantage.
entries.pool_title: Randomized Clustered Nystrom for Large-Scale Kernel Machines
entries.title: Randomized Clustered Nystrom for Large-Scale Kernel Machines

entries.difference: Reduces the variance of random-feature couplings; a refinement of the classical surrogate family that the field's residual advantages are usually measured against.
entries.pool_title: Variance-Reducing Couplings for Random Features
entries.title: Variance-Reducing Couplings for Random Features

entries.difference: Constructs simplex random features with lower variance; another refinement of the weak surrogate, and we include the family as our weak-rival control.
entries.pool_title: Simplex Random Features
entries.title: Simplex Random Features

entries.authors: Sernau, L., Bonacina, S., Saurous, R.
entries.difference: Shows all random-feature representations are equivalent; the equivalence explains why a random-feature rival cannot exploit a specific geometry, which is why our headline rival is not of that family.
entries.pool_title: All Random Features Representations are Equivalent
entries.title: All Random Features Representations Are Equivalent

entries.authors: Aguirre-López, F., Franz, S., Pastore, M.
entries.difference: Studies random features and polynomial rules; a spectral analysis of an approximation family, with no quantum arm.
entries.pool_title: Random features and polynomial rules
entries.title: Random Features and Polynomial Rules

entries.difference: Frames quantum random features as a spectral framework for quantum machine learning; a spectral view of quantum maps, with no matched-rival comparison of test error.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Random Features: A Spectral Framework for Quantum Machine Learning
entries.title: Quantum Random Features: A Spectral Framework for Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Estimates dynamic models by matching random features; an econometric matching argument that supports our use of a matching construction for the rival's metric.
entries.pool_title: Estimating dynamic models by matching random features
entries.title: Estimating Dynamic Models by Matching Random Features

entries.difference: Gives a scalable Nyström-based kernel two-sample test with permutations; a classical testing instrument, cited for the resampling practice our protocol follows.
entries.pool_title: A Scalable Nystrom-Based Kernel Two-Sample Test with Permutations
entries.title: A Scalable Nystrom-Based Kernel Two-Sample Test with Permutations

entries.difference: Uses graph random features for scalable Gaussian processes; a classical scalability result for the baseline family we tune against the quantum maps.
entries.pool_title: Graph Random Features for Scalable Gaussian Processes
entries.title: Graph Random Features for Scalable Gaussian Processes

entries.difference: Develops random features for Grassmannian kernels; a geometry-specific classical approximation, cited to show that geometry-aware classical constructions are available outside the quantum setting.
entries.pool_title: Random Features for Grassmannian Kernels
entries.title: Random Features for Grassmannian Kernels

entries.difference: Regularises cross-validation for stability; a selection-side remedy, whereas our protocol fixes the selection rule and reports the comparison's uncertainty.
entries.pool_title: Stability Regularized Cross-Validation
entries.title: Stability Regularized Cross-Validation

entries.authors: Gauran, I., Ombao, H., Yu, Z.
entries.difference: Tests predictive performance with exhaustive nested cross-validation for high-dimensional data; a testing procedure, which we cite for the nested-CV discipline our rival's tuning follows.
entries.pool_title: Predictive Performance Test based on the Exhaustive Nested Cross-Validation for High-dimensional data
entries.title: Predictive Performance Test Based on the Exhaustive Nested Cross-Validation for High-Dimensional Data

entries.difference: Calibrates multiple testing without labels; a calibration method for testing procedures, related to our null calibration but not to the kernel comparison.
entries.pool_title: Calibration without labels in multiple testing
entries.title: Calibration Without Labels in Multiple Testing

entries.difference: Unifies conformalised multiple testing with full data efficiency; a testing framework, cited for the family of procedures our declaration rule belongs to.
entries.pool_title: Unified Conformalized Multiple Testing with Full Data Efficiency
entries.title: Unified Conformalized Multiple Testing with Full Data Efficiency

entries.difference: Controls the false discovery rate through a bandit formulation; an online multiple-testing method, from which our fixed-grid FDR control differs by design.
entries.pool_title: A Bandit Approach to Multiple Testing with False Discovery Control
entries.title: A Bandit Approach to Multiple Testing with False Discovery Control

entries.authors: Rabinovich, M., Jordan, M., Wainwright, M.
entries.difference: Gives lower bounds in multiple testing through derandomised proxies; it bounds what any procedure of our kind can detect, which is why we report the declaration count's saturation as a finding.
entries.pool_title: Lower bounds in multiple testing: A framework based on derandomized proxies
entries.title: Lower Bounds in Multiple Testing: A Framework Based on Derandomized Proxies

entries.authors: Martinez-Taboada, D., Chugg, B., Ramdas, A.
entries.difference: Derives Bentkus-type asymptotic e-values; a calibration result for e-value tests, cited as the modern alternative to the p-value layer we use.
entries.pool_title: Bentkus-type asymptotic e-values
entries.title: Bentkus-Type Asymptotic E-Values

entries.difference: Gives dynamic algorithms for online multiple testing; an online setting, whereas our grid is fixed before the run.
entries.pool_title: Dynamic Algorithms for Online Multiple Testing
entries.title: Dynamic Algorithms for Online Multiple Testing

entries.difference: Proposes a robust multiple-testing method that leverages ancillary information; a shrinkage-style improvement, which we cite for why null calibration matters in our own predictive null.
entries.pool_title: DART2: a robust multiple testing method to smartly leverage helpful or misleading ancillary information
entries.title: DART2: A Robust Multiple Testing Method to Smartly Leverage Helpful or Misleading Ancillary Information

entries.difference: Bilevel optimisation for learning hyperparameters; a joint tuning scheme, cited for the nested protocol our rival's envelope grid follows.
entries.pool_title: Bilevel optimization for learning hyperparameters: Application to solving PDEs and inverse problems with Gaussian processes
entries.title: Bilevel Optimization for Learning Hyperparameters: Application to Solving PDEs and Inverse Problems with Gaussian Processes

entries.authors: Kam, C., Bessafi, M., Cadet, F.
entries.difference: Shows structured features overfit where random features grok; a mechanism for why a rival's family choice interacts with the data's structure, which our grid controls.
entries.pool_title: Structured Features Overfit Where Random Features Grok
entries.title: Structured Features Overfit Where Random Features Grok

entries.authors: Joshi, S., Mendes, U., Govia, L.
entries.difference: Balances expressivity and overfitting in quantum Gaussian-process regression; a single-model balance, with no rival receiving the model's metric.
entries.pool_title: Balancing Expressivity and Overfitting in Quantum Gaussian Process Regression
entries.title: Balancing Expressivity and Overfitting in Quantum Gaussian Process Regression

entries.difference: Introduced manifold random features; a classical construction that makes a data-geometry-aware rival available outside the quantum setting.
entries.pool_title: Manifold Random Features
entries.title: Manifold Random Features

entries.difference: Applies quantum-enhanced manifold learning to anomaly recognition; an application whose classical comparison is unmatched.
entries.pool_title: Q-BAR: Blogger Anomaly Recognition via Quantum-enhanced Manifold Learning
entries.title: Q-BAR: Blogger Anomaly Recognition via Quantum-Enhanced Manifold Learning

entries.difference: Builds a hybrid pipeline for parity-structured classification with quantum kernels; a pipeline for one structure, whereas our generator sweeps the alignment between structure and map.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernels for Parity-Structured Classification: A Hybrid Pipeline
entries.title: Quantum Kernels for Parity-Structured Classification: A Hybrid Pipeline

entries.difference: Designs structured quantum kernels for chaotic forecasting; a forecasting task whose evaluation is against classical forecasters with different capacity.
entries.pool_title: Structured Quantum Kernels for Chaotic Forecasting
entries.title: Structured Quantum Kernels for Chaotic Forecasting

entries.difference: Derives barren plateaus from learning scramblers with local cost functions; a variational mechanism result cited for why our large-bandwidth arm is read as collapse rather than as a tuning failure.
entries.pool_title: Barren plateaus from learning scramblers with local cost functions
entries.title: Barren Plateaus from Learning Scramblers with Local Cost Functions

entries.authors: Rodriguez-Grasa, P., Ban, Y., Sanz, M.
entries.difference: Trains quantum kernels with quantum neural networks; it moves the map to improve performance, while we fix the map and compare against a rival built from its metric.
entries.pool_title: Neural quantum kernels: training quantum kernels with quantum neural networks
entries.title: Neural Quantum Kernels: Training Quantum Kernels with Quantum Neural Networks

entries.difference: Estimates expectation values efficiently with extended stabilizer frameworks and adaptive variance estimation; it measures how cheaply a quantum model can be evaluated, not how it compares with a matched classical rival.
entries.pool_title: Efficient expectation value estimation for quantum circuits via extended stabilizer frameworks and adaptive variance estimation
entries.title: Efficient Expectation Value Estimation for Quantum Circuits via Extended Stabilizer Frameworks and Adaptive Variance Estimation

entries.authors: Pal, P., Sharma, G., Podila, R.
entries.difference: Certifies quantum advantage robustly against loopholes; a certification protocol for advantage claims, cited as the standard our controlled comparison is not.
entries.pool_title: Loophole-Robust Certification of Quantum Advantage
entries.title: Loophole-Robust Certification of Quantum Advantage

entries.difference: Studies quantum advantage in tolerant junta testing; a query-complexity separation, which is an advantage of a different kind from the statistical one we map.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Advantage in Tolerant Junta Testing
entries.title: Quantum Advantage in Tolerant Junta Testing

entries.difference: Characterises the power of noisy quantum kernels; noise is the axis, and our study is noiseless by construction, so it isolates the geometric question.
entries.pool_title: Power Characterization of Noisy Quantum Kernels
entries.title: Power Characterization of Noisy Quantum Kernels

entries.authors: Paine, A., Elfving, V., Kyriienko, O.
entries.difference: Solves differential equations with quantum kernel methods; a solver application whose classical comparison is a numerical baseline, not a matched kernel.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Kernel Methods for Solving Differential Equations
entries.title: Quantum Kernel Methods for Solving Differential Equations

entries.authors: Ahmad, S., Rawat, R., Moharir, M.
entries.difference: Uses non-classically simulable feature maps in hybrid quantum-classical architectures; the map is chosen for hardness, whereas we choose maps we can read exactly so the geometry is computable.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Machine Learning with HQC Architectures using non-Classically Simulable Feature Maps
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning with HQC Architectures Using Non-Classically Simulable Feature Maps

entries.difference: Studies noisy quantum kernel machines; a noise-focused study, cited because our noiseless design is what makes the metric computable in closed form.
entries.pool_title: Noisy Quantum Kernel Machines
entries.title: Noisy Quantum Kernel Machines

entries.difference: Builds a compact quantum kernel-based binary classifier for near-term hardware; a hardware-oriented construction evaluated against unmatched classical baselines.
entries.pool_title: Compact quantum kernel-based binary classifier
entries.title: Compact Quantum Kernel-Based Binary Classifier

entries.difference: Studies Fisher efficiency transitions for non-unitary quantum machine learning; an information-theoretic transition, cited as an example of a boundary derived rather than mapped.
entries.pool_title: Non-Unitary Quantum Machine Learning: Fisher Efficiency Transitions from Distributed Quantum Expressivity
entries.title: Non-Unitary Quantum Machine Learning: Fisher Efficiency Transitions from Distributed Quantum Expressivity

entries.difference: Applies quantum machine learning to cyber-physical anomaly detection in unmanned aerial vehicles; an application whose evaluation varies many factors at once.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Machine Learning for Cyber-Physical Anomaly Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Leakage-Free Evaluation with Proxy-Audited Feature Sets
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Cyber-Physical Anomaly Detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicles: A Leakage-Free Evaluation with Proxy-Audited Feature Sets

entries.difference: Compares array frameworks for quantum-circuit simulation; a runtime comparison of simulators, which is the cost axis our reproduction spec reports honestly.
entries.pool_title: Qupertino: Pure MLX Array Kernels versus Hand-Tuned Metal Shaders for Quantum Circuit Simulation on Apple Silicon
entries.title: Qupertino: Pure MLX Array Kernels Versus Hand-Tuned Metal Shaders for Quantum Circuit Simulation on Apple Silicon

entries.difference: Simulates observable quantum dynamics on dynamic subspaces; a fast-simulation technique that bounds the cost of the exact statevector path we use at q <= 8.
entries.pool_title: Dynamic Observable Subspaces: Fast Simulation of Observable Quantum Dynamics
entries.title: Dynamic Observable Subspaces: Fast Simulation of Observable Quantum Dynamics

entries.difference: Prepares tensor-network states with belief-propagation disentanglers; a state preparation technique, cited as an alternative to exact statevector simulation.
entries.pool_title: Belief Propagation-based Disentanglers for Tensor Network State Preparation
entries.title: Belief Propagation-Based Disentanglers for Tensor Network State Preparation

entries.authors: Manabe, H., Sugimoto, T., Fujii, K.
entries.difference: Formulates dequantized algorithms in tensor-network language; a formulation that explains when classical simulation is exact, which our closed-form rival does for the small-bandwidth regime.
entries.pool_title: Tensor Network Formulation of Dequantized Algorithms for Ground State Energy Estimation
entries.title: Tensor Network Formulation of Dequantized Algorithms for Ground State Energy Estimation

entries.difference: Compares supervised classifiers over multiple data sets with paired tests and recommends a procedure; a testing protocol, where our contribution is the map of a comparison's outcome rather than a test for it.
entries.pool_title: Approximate Statistical Tests for Comparing Supervised Classification Learning Algorithms
entries.title: Approximate Statistical Tests for Comparing Supervised Classification Learning Algorithms

entries.difference: Measures the bias that cross-validation introduces when it is also used for selection; the bias our rival's nested protocol is designed to remove, cited as the reason the nested grid is part of the rival definition.
entries.pool_title: Bias in error estimation when using cross-validation for model selection
entries.title: Bias in Error Estimation When Using Cross-Validation for Model Selection

entries.difference: Introduces the false discovery rate and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure; the declaration rule we apply to our grid before any lead is announced.
entries.pool_title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
entries.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
entries.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society Series B: Statistical Methodology

entries.difference: Extends false-discovery control to dependent test statistics; the dependency our grid's tests have by construction, which is why the control is reported with its structure rather than as a bare count.
entries.pool_title: The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency
entries.title: The Control of the False Discovery Rate in Multiple Testing under Dependency

entries.difference: Gives the small-sample paired statistic and its distribution; the t-interval we report per cell across the stream panel.
entries.pool_title: The Probable Error of a Mean
entries.title: The Probable Error of a Mean

entries.difference: Argues for the algorithmic-modelling culture against the data-modelling one; the argument for controlled generators, which is the design this study uses.
entries.pool_title: Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures (with comments and a rejoinder by the author)
entries.title: Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures (with Comments and a Rejoinder by the Author)

entries.difference: Shows no learner is a priori superior without assumptions on the problem distribution; the reason a comparison must name the geometry it holds fixed, as ours does.
entries.pool_title: The Lack of A Priori Distinctions Between Learning Algorithms
entries.title: The Lack of a Priori Distinctions Between Learning Algorithms

entries.difference: Introduces locally weighted regression and its smoothing parameter; an early statement that a nonparametric fit's bandwidth decides its behaviour, the axis our grid sweeps for the quantum map.
entries.pool_title: Robust Locally Weighted Regression and Smoothing Scatterplots
entries.title: Robust Locally Weighted Regression and Smoothing Scatterplots
entries.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

entries.difference: Establishes the theory of reproducing kernels; the framework in which a kernel is a metric, which is what makes a metric-matched rival meaningful.
entries.pool_title: Theory of Reproducing Kernels.
entries.title: Theory of Reproducing Kernels.

entries.difference: Sets out kernel methods for pattern analysis as a design discipline; the classical toolbox our rival arms are drawn from.
entries.pool_title: Kernel Methods for Pattern Analysis
entries.title: Kernel Methods for Pattern Analysis

entries.difference: Gives the positive-definite condition for a function to be a kernel; the condition our rival metrics must satisfy for the comparison to be between kernels at all.
entries.pool_title: Functions of positive and negative type, and their connection with the theory of integral equations
entries.title: Functions of Positive and Negative Type, and Their Connection with the Theory of Integral Equations
entries.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Containing Papers of a Mathematical and Physical Character

entries.difference: Introduces the kernel trick for optimal margin classifiers; the construction that makes a geometry and a hypothesis class separable questions.
entries.pool_title: A training algorithm for optimal margin classifiers
entries.title: A Training Algorithm for Optimal Margin Classifiers
entries.venue: Proceedings of the fifth annual workshop on Computational learning theory

entries.difference: Introduces support-vector networks with soft margins; the classifier family our arms are scored inside, through kernel ridge regression with a linear readout.
entries.pool_title: Support-Vector Networks
entries.title: Support-Vector Networks

entries.difference: Chooses multiple kernel parameters by gradient descent on a generalisation bound; an early statement that kernel parameters are themselves a fitting problem, which our nested envelope grid implements.
entries.pool_title: Choosing Multiple Parameters for Support Vector Machines
entries.title: Choosing Multiple Parameters for Support Vector Machines

entries.difference: Learns a combination of kernels through conic duality; the multiple-kernel setting in which a rival's metric is chosen rather than given, cited to delimit what our fixed-metric rival claims.
entries.pool_title: Multiple kernel learning, conic duality, and the SMO algorithm
entries.title: Multiple Kernel Learning, Conic Duality, and the SMO Algorithm
entries.venue: Twenty-first international conference on Machine learning - ICML '04

entries.difference: Introduces kernel principal component analysis; a classical use of a kernel's geometry, cited to show that geometry exploitation is not peculiar to the quantum setting.
entries.pool_title: Nonlinear Component Analysis as a Kernel Eigenvalue Problem
entries.title: Nonlinear Component Analysis as a Kernel Eigenvalue Problem

entries.difference: Introduces natural-gradient learning; the geometry-aware optimisation idea that our rival's metric-matching transfers to regression.
entries.pool_title: Natural Gradient Works Efficiently in Learning
entries.title: Natural Gradient Works Efficiently in Learning

entries.difference: Introduces random forests; a strong classical baseline of a different family, included so the manuscript's baseline claim is not confined to kernel machines.
entries.pool_title: Random Forests
entries.title: Random Forests

entries.authors: Geurts, P., Ernst, D., Wehenkel, L.
entries.difference: Introduces extremely randomized trees; a second tree-family baseline, cited for the same reason as random forests.
entries.pool_title: Extremely randomized trees
entries.title: Extremely Randomized Trees

entries.difference: Applies gradient-based learning to document recognition; a reference for the conventional machine-learning baselines a kernel comparison should acknowledge.
entries.pool_title: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition
entries.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition

entries.difference: Relates precision-recall and ROC curves; the reason our reported metric is excess risk against the Bayes predictor rather than an accuracy curve.
entries.pool_title: The relationship between Precision-Recall and ROC curves
entries.title: The Relationship Between Precision-Recall and ROC Curves
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd international conference on Machine learning - ICML '06

entries.difference: States the uniform convergence of empirical frequencies used throughout learning theory; the capacity view that motivates controlling the rival's envelope grid.
entries.pool_title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events to Their Probabilities
entries.title: On the Uniform Convergence of Relative Frequencies of Events to Their Probabilities

entries.difference: Proves convergence properties of the EM algorithm; a classical estimation-theory landmark, cited to mark how far a fitted-metric rival is from a construction with a closed-form metric.
entries.pool_title: On the Convergence Properties of the EM Algorithm
entries.title: On the Convergence Properties of the EM Algorithm

entries.authors: Rumelhart, D., Hinton, G., Williams, R.
entries.difference: Shows learning by back-propagation; the historical baseline that motivates holding capacity fixed across the arms of a comparison.
entries.pool_title: Learning representations by back-propagating errors
entries.title: Learning Representations by Back-Propagating Errors

entries.difference: Describes the NISQ era and its constraints; the hardware setting the field's advantage claims are made in, and the reason an exactly simulated comparison is informative.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Computing in the NISQ era and beyond
entries.title: Quantum Computing in the NISQ Era and Beyond

entries.difference: States the universal quantum computer and its relation to the Church-Turing principle; the foundational statement of what a quantum computation is.
entries.pool_title: Quantum theory, the Church–Turing principle and the universal quantum computer
entries.title: Quantum Theory, the Church–Turing Principle and the Universal Quantum Computer
entries.venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. A. Mathematical and Physical Sciences

entries.difference: Surveys quantum machine learning as a discipline; the field-level framing our matched-rival comparison argues within.
entries.pool_title: Quantum machine learning
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning

entries.difference: Demonstrates supervised learning with quantum-enhanced feature spaces on hardware; the experiment that established the quantum-kernel advantage claim our study subjects to a matched rival.
entries.pool_title: Supervised learning with quantum-enhanced feature spaces
entries.title: Supervised Learning with Quantum-Enhanced Feature Spaces

entries.difference: Puts quantum machine learning in feature Hilbert spaces; the formal setting in which a feature map is a kernel, which our instrument computes exactly.
entries.pool_title: Quantum Machine Learning in Feature Hilbert Spaces
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning in Feature Hilbert Spaces

entries.difference: Analyses the power of quantum kernels in the NISQ era and shows where classical data defeats them; the closest prior argument, stated for specific constructions rather than as a mapped advantage region.
entries.pool_title: Towards understanding the power of quantum kernels in the NISQ era
entries.title: Towards Understanding the Power of Quantum Kernels in the NISQ Era

entries.difference: Demonstrates quantum advantage in learning from experiments; an advantage of a different kind (sample access), cited to separate it from the test-error advantage we map.
entries.pool_title: Quantum advantage in learning from experiments
entries.title: Quantum Advantage in Learning from Experiments

entries.difference: Shows barren plateaus are absent in quantum convolutional neural networks with local cost functions; the architectural escape from collapse, cited against our large-bandwidth arm.
entries.pool_title: Absence of Barren Plateaus in Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks
entries.title: Absence of Barren Plateaus in Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks

entries.authors: Cong, I., Choi, S., Lukin, M.
entries.difference: Introduces quantum convolutional neural networks; a variational architecture, included so the manuscript's map is not read as a statement about all quantum models.
entries.pool_title: Quantum convolutional neural networks
entries.title: Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks

entries.difference: Shows exponential concentration in quantum kernel methods and ties it to the kernel's spectrum; the concentration result our large-bandwidth arm reproduces as a comparison outcome.
entries.pool_title: Exponential concentration in quantum kernel methods
entries.title: Exponential Concentration in Quantum Kernel Methods

entries.difference: Applies quantum machine learning to quantum anomaly detection; an early kernel application whose comparison is against classical kernels of a different metric.
entries.pool_title: Quantum machine learning for quantum anomaly detection
entries.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Quantum Anomaly Detection

entries.authors: Wang, D., Higgott, O., Brierley, S.
entries.difference: Accelerates the variational quantum eigensolver; an optimisation result, cited to contrast optimisation gains with the statistical comparison this study makes.
entries.pool_title: Accelerated Variational Quantum Eigensolver
entries.title: Accelerated Variational Quantum Eigensolver

entries.difference: Describes a simulation environment for compartmental neuron models; a computational-neuroscience tool, cited only as an instance of the simulator-versus-model distinction our threats section draws.
entries.pool_title: Expanding NEURON's Repertoire of Mechanisms with NMODL
entries.title: Expanding NEURON's Repertoire of Mechanisms with NMODL

entries.difference: Introduces Laplacian eigenmaps; a spectral embedding whose graph-Laplacian operator is the classical object our closed-form rival's metric is built from.
entries.pool_title: Laplacian Eigenmaps for Dimensionality Reduction and Data Representation
entries.title: Laplacian Eigenmaps for Dimensionality Reduction and Data Representation

entries.difference: Develops confirmatory maximum-likelihood factor analysis; a latent-structure method, cited as an example of a model whose geometry is fixed by construction rather than fitted.
entries.pool_title: A General Approach to Confirmatory Maximum Likelihood Factor Analysis
entries.title: A General Approach to Confirmatory Maximum Likelihood Factor Analysis

entries.difference: Gives sparse multinomial logistic regression with fast algorithms; a capacity-controlled classifier, cited for the envelope discipline our rival's grid imposes.
entries.pool_title: Sparse multinomial logistic regression: fast algorithms and generalization bounds
entries.title: Sparse Multinomial Logistic Regression: Fast Algorithms and Generalization Bounds
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence

entries.difference: Learns structured predictors discriminatively and without labels; a semi-supervised construction, cited to delimit what our supervised comparison covers.
entries.pool_title: Discriminative unsupervised learning of structured predictors
entries.title: Discriminative Unsupervised Learning of Structured Predictors
entries.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd international conference on Machine learning - ICML '06

entries.authors: Ritchie, A., Teufel, S., Robertson, S.
entries.difference: Uses citation terms for information retrieval; a term-selection study, cited as the method this package's reference search does not use.
entries.pool_title: Using Terms from Citations for IR: Some First Results
entries.title: Using Terms from Citations for IR: Some First Results

entries.difference: Self-tests multipartite entangled states; a certification protocol for entanglement, cited as the kind of guarantee that a statistical advantage claim does not by itself carry.
entries.pool_title: Self-testing of multipartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger states of arbitrary local dimension with arbitrary number of measurements per party
entries.title: Self-Testing of Multipartite Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger States of Arbitrary Local Dimension with Arbitrary Number of Measurements per Party

entries.difference: Simulates imaginary-time evolution with a variational ansatz; a variational quantum algorithm, cited as background for the ansatz-based maps our grid does not use.
entries.pool_title: Variational ansatz-based quantum simulation of imaginary time evolution
entries.title: Variational Ansatz-Based Quantum Simulation of Imaginary Time Evolution
